summary.headline: Reliance Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA hit a record Rs 62,409 crore (+24% YoY) and PAT crossed Rs 50,000 crore on a half-year basis, led by O2C.
summary.overview: Consolidated EBITDA rose 24% YoY to Rs 62,409 crore and PAT rose 34% to close to Rs 30,000 crore, both records for the company. O2C EBITDA rose 69% to Rs 25,203 crore on tight product markets, wide ethane-naphtha spreads and record crude runs, despite higher freight, insurance and crude premiums. Digital services EBITDA rose 18% to about Rs 22,200 crore, while Retail EBITDA fell about 10-11% to Rs 6,228 crore as it invests in online commerce. Management said the first-half run-rate points to annualised O2C EBITDA well above Rs 80,000 crore, though it cautioned that the earnings benefit is driven by geopolitical disruption.

segments.name: O2C (Oil to Chemicals)
segments.commentary: EBITDA Rs 25,203 crore, up 69% YoY, the strongest quarter seen. Gasoline cracks about 3x YoY, diesel about 3.5x, jet about 3.7x; ethane-naphtha differential at $557/t, up 2.3x YoY. Management expects FY27 O2C EBITDA of about Rs 80,000 crore.

segments.name: Jio Platforms
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 40,475 crore (+11.4% YoY), EBITDA Rs 21,879 crore (+16.6%), subscribers 542 million with 36 million net adds over 12 months, 300 million 5G users, 30 million homes connected; ARPU Rs 218.8 (+3.5% YoY without tariff hike). IPO listed at 26.7% premium, making it second-largest listed company by market cap.

segments.name: Reliance Retail
segments.commentary: Revenue +6.4% YoY, EBITDA Rs 6,228 crore (-11% YoY), margin 7.8%, down 140 bps YoY. Registered customers above 400 million (+10%); 303 stores opened and about 500 closed; online grocery revenue +42% YoY; ~20,000 stores, 77.5 million sq ft. Margin hit from online investment and price parity in quick commerce.

segments.name: Reliance Consumer Products (FMCG)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 8,266 crore (1.6x YoY); H1 Rs 16,900 crore (1.8x YoY). Entered ice cream via Bombay Creamery; presence expanded to Australia (Coles, Woolworths), Kenya and GCC/SE Asia markets.

segments.name: JioStar
segments.commentary: Total MAU on JioHotstar 440 million (+10% YoY); revenue +10% YoY, driven by D2C subscriptions and linear TV. Sports monetisation was weak early in the quarter due to Middle East overhang, improving by India-West Indies series; Drishyam 3 crossed Rs 500 crore global box office.

segments.name: Exploration and Production
segments.commentary: Production broadly flat QoQ; KG-D6 decline offset by higher gas prices and CBM uptrend. Gas ceiling price for the half raised by $1 to about $9.9/mmBtu. A deepwater rig returned to KG-D6 for workovers and development wells.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 O2C EBITDA of about Rs 80,000 crore, based on H1 tracking well above that annualised rate.
Retail: investment year in FY27; management says online economics improve from FY28 and benefits show in absolute EBITDA; target to double operating EBITDA in about two years is unchanged.

New energy: earnings contribution expected from FY28; module capacity 6+ GW now, targeting 20 GW early next year; solar cell about 5 GW now, targeting 20 GW in H1 CY27; BESS (40 GWh) commissioning next half, cell capacity (35-40 GWh) around late next year.
Jio capex tapering as 5G and UBR core network deployment completes; strong cash flow expected over the next several quarters.
Global oil demand projected to fall about 2.5-2.6 mb/d in 2026 and rebound 2-2.3 mb/d in 2027 (IEA), per management.
Three new ethane carriers: first operating, second on its way to US, third due shortly.
capex_capacity: Refinery utilisation at record crude runs despite Strait of Hormuz disruptions; coker, platformer and FCC running at high levels.
Ethane carrier fleet: one of three new vessels operating, second delivered and en route to US, third due shortly.
Data centre: 44 MW being completed over the next four to six months; plan for another 120 MW later; infra build for a hyperscaler customer.
Retail: 303 stores opened, about 500 unviable stores shut; retail area down about 1 million sq ft to 77.5 million sq ft; warehousing space flat.
Net debt-to-EBITDA ratio cited around 0.47 for September 2026; capex described as broadly flat QoQ.
demand_pricing: Brent ranged $70-130/bbl over the quarter; Q2 average $97 vs $69 pre-conflict. Physical crude premiums and freight rates elevated, raising OpEx.
Domestic fuel demand strong: MS +8.5% YoY, diesel +7.5% YoY, helped by deficient monsoon and under-recovery pricing.
Global polymer capacity impacted: PE, MEG and PTA together roughly 25-30% of global capacity affected; global cracker utilisation fell from 81% to 71%.
Naphtha availability from Middle East halved; naphtha AG-Japan freight rose from $86/t in July to $186/t in September.
Domestic polymer demand down 3% YoY on supply constraints; Jio ARPU up 3.5% YoY without tariff increase.
Jio fixed wireless holds over 78% share with 15.1 million connections.
Retail: online grocery share up 270 bps YoY; electronics distribution +20% YoY; premium phones strongly up; own brands up 710 bps share in apparel.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 5 million barrels/day of refinery capacity still offline likely to normalise in 6-9 months, and what if it takes longer?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed with the framing: remaining outages are in Russia (about 40% of capacity concerned) and Middle East refineries still ramping. No resolution is visible given ongoing attacks, so no near-term change is expected.

qa_highlights.question: How is crude sourcing being positioned given Middle East flows recovering?
qa_highlights.answer: Sourcing is switched month to month between East and West of Suez to chase the most advantageous crude; this approach continues into October-December.

qa_highlights.question: What drove O2C profit growth QoQ: refining, petchem or the new ethane carriers?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined effect. Petchem contributed, refining also; diesel up about $2.8/bbl QoQ; time-chartered fleet mitigated freight; gasifier benefited from high gas prices; product premiums also helped.

qa_highlights.question: Is the demand decline in China structural, and will refining margins fall below prior normal levels?
qa_highlights.answer: China's EV and LNG-truck shift is structural, but rest-of-world demand should more than offset it; management expects a strong 2027 rebound. It sees margins staying elevated because the market's memory of supply shocks will persist, not a normalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Commissioning timelines for new energy lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Module capacity at 6+ GW rising to 20 GW early next year; solar cell about 5 GW rising to 20 GW in H1 CY27; BESS in the next calendar half and cell from June to December; transmission connectivity by Q1 next year; revenue expected in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Retail: when do investments taper and what is the margin trajectory? Plus data centre capex and IPL bid.
qa_highlights.answer: Competition remains intense; online margins structurally lower due to discounts and delivery costs; benefits expected from FY28 onwards. Data centre 44 MW in 4-6 months, 120 MW planned later. Management is keen to bid for IPL rights, with price discipline.

qa_highlights.question: Does a double-EBITDA target in two years still hold given weak online growth vs quick commerce peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail says the target is unchanged. Online growth is measured and funded from the existing 400 million customer base; economics should improve from next year.

qa_highlights.question: Has O2C spread capture improved, and will the two new vessels add further?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Petchem volumes improved as LPG control order relaxed; refining feedstock capture improved with regional switching; ethane advantage to grow with the incremental vessels.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 6,228 crore (7.8% margin, before Rs 108 crore exceptional)
about Rs 90,000 crore run-rate basis, revenue growth 6.4%

risks_watch: Refinery outages: about 4-5 mb/d of capacity still offline (Russia and Middle East), with no resolution visible; any normalisation timing remains uncertain.

Retail margin trajectory: EBITDA down about 11% YoY with margin at 7.8% (down 140 bps YoY); benefits guided only from FY28, and the double-EBITDA-in-two-years target is unchanged but depends on online economics improving.

O2C earnings dependent on geopolitical tightness and elevated cracks; management expects margins to stay elevated, while Middle East naphtha flows, freight and insurance costs and Russian refinery attacks remain volatile.
New energy execution: module capacity 6+ GW to 20 GW early next year, solar cell 5 GW to 20 GW in H1 CY27, BESS and cell ramp (June to December), with revenue guided from FY28.
Jio capex tapering as 5G and UBR deployment completes; cash flow inflection expected over the next several quarters. Watch IPL rights tender (renewal early 2027) and bid discipline.
Domestic under-recoveries, SAED levy and LPG production curtailment weighing on margins and polymer demand (down 3% YoY), which could affect the sustainability of the O2C run-rate.
key_quotes: So, O2C led the charge with EBITDA up 68%.
So, the strategy has remained unchanged from what we said in the last quarter.
So, we are very, very constructive.
The answer is absolutely yes. At what price? That is a different one.

summary.management_tone: Confident and constructive on O2C, describing the outlook as structurally positive and FY27 O2C EBITDA of about Rs 80,000 crore as tracking well. Cautious on geopolitics, saying there is no visible resolution and uncertainty is very high, and defensive on Retail, framing the margin decline as a deliberate, time-bound investment year.
